_doc: Object layer of the aerial encode. Paths are relative to the repo root. coco.keep: the COCO classes that can occur in aerial footage (indoor and household classes are what a closed vocabulary emits for objects it has no name for). world.prompts: YOLO-World prompt -> index token; the .onnx is exported with exactly these prompts, in this order (run.sh does it). merge_iou: overlapping boxes from either head are one object; the more confident label wins. track: an object in the next kept frame is the same object at IoU >= iou when the two crops look alike (HSV histogram correlation >= min_appearance; this is what stops a track jumping a cut) and the two labels are in one group (heads swap labels inside a group: truck/tank/boat), across up to max_gap missed frames. A label in no group is its own group. The object's class is the confidence-weighted vote over its frames. text: scene text is an object class. Tesseract (page segmentation psm) only locates it: words with conf >= min_conf that look like a stencil, grouped into lines, become 'text' boxes; Florence reads them. A text box at least host_containment inside another object's box gives that object its words (AMMO on a truck); one with no host (NORTH GATE) stays an object of its own; one Florence reads as empty is dropped. ocr: each object is read on up to `views` crops spread over its frames (the largest view is often not the one showing the lettering), and the words are merged; classes in skip are not read.
